:::{#exm-function}
#### Doubling a die roll

The rule $f(a) = 2a$ defines a function $f : \set{1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6} \to \reals$,
because it assigns exactly one real number to each possible roll;
for example, $f(3) = 6$.
A rule that assigned both $2$ and $-2$ to the roll $1$
would not be a function,
because a function assigns exactly one value to each element.

:::
